home.live.title: Run it yourself
home.live.lede: CIND3R3LLA is free software under the GNU Affero General Public License v3.0. Read every line, run it on your own infrastructure, and modify it. An archive asks a community for trust, and the licence is what makes that trust checkable rather than promised.
home.how.title: A control plane for intelligent identities
home.how.lede: CIND3R3LLA is a self hosted control plane for intelligent identities inside private and public communities. It brings the embedded core, deterministic application logic, local language models, persistent community memory, human supervision, moderation workflows, knowledge publishing and character driven interaction together in one platform, running on hardware you control.
home.tile.csam.title: CSAM screening (in development)
home.tile.csam.body: The pipeline is built to hash every image and video at receipt and compare it against databases of known abuse material, holding any match for the authorities rather than deleting it. The screening stage is in development and no detection provider is connected yet, so no such check runs today. Hash matching finds known material only; it cannot detect new material.
home.tile.consent.title: Consent-first
home.tile.consent.body: Nothing passes through without the group's explicit opt-in. Consent is checked before capture, never assumed, and can be withdrawn at any time.
home.tile.secure.title: Secure by design
home.tile.secure.body: Passwordless passkeys, encrypted transport, media behind authentication, full audit logging. Security is the foundation, not an add-on.
home.tile.archived.title: Then archived
home.tile.archived.body: Only what clears screening becomes a permanent, searchable public record. Everything else simply never appears.
home.suite.title: What the platform does
home.suite.lede: The consent first archive is one capability among several, not the product.
home.suite.archive.title: Public web archive
home.suite.archive.body: Consent-gated capture, full-text search, filters, infinite scroll, video playback, and SEO-friendly public pages. Built to make a community's shared knowledge findable for years, not buried in chat history.
home.suite.roadmap.title: On the roadmap
home.sec.title: Part of the architecture, not a checkbox
home.sec.lede: Passkeys as the primary administrative login, an admin console bound to loopback behind TLS, originals encrypted at rest, metadata stripped before publication, and every state changing action written to an audit trail.
home.sec.point1: Passkeys first, with a break glass path the operator controls
home.sec.point2: Media originals encrypted at rest, public copies stripped of metadata
home.sec.point3: Consent enforced in the database view, not in a flag somebody can forget
home.sec.point4: Audit coverage on every administrative action
demo.consent: Every group opted in. Withdraw anytime.

features.lede: A firewall pipeline: consent first, then screening, and only then the public archive. Consent is enforced in code today. The screening stage is in development.
features.cap1.title: Consent-gated capture
features.cap1.body: The bot joins a public group and asks before anything is read. Capture starts only after an explicit opt-in, and stops the moment consent is withdrawn. Every opt-in and opt-out is recorded, so the archive can always prove why a message is there.
features.cap2.title: CSAM & content screening (in development)
features.cap2.body: The heart of the firewall: every image and video is hashed and checked against known-abuse databases before it can be stored. Flagged media is blocked and never reaches the archive. The operator sees it in a review queue, nowhere else.
features.cap3.title: The public web archive
features.cap3.body: Only what clears screening is published. What remains becomes permanent public pages: full-text search across every message, filters by group, author, date and media, infinite scroll, inline video, and SEO-friendly stable URLs. Search engines index it, people actually find it.
features.cap4.title: Reporting & moderation
features.cap4.body: A second line after screening: anyone can report a published message. Reports reach the operator's console for review, takedown, and audit. Moderation is a first-class workflow, not an afterthought.
features.roadmap.title: Planned capabilities
features.roadmap.lede: In development or design. Order and scope may change, because this is alpha software and we would rather ship the safeguards first.
features.rm.matrix.body: The same consent-first archive and bot suite for Matrix rooms.

features.rm.videogallery.body: A dedicated browsing surface for archived video and images.
features.rm.moderation.body: Bulk actions, policies, and reviewer queues.
features.rm.localai.body: Screening and summaries that run on your own hardware.

security.lede: CIND3R3LLA is a consent firewall: nothing is published unless its author asked for it. This page explains how that is enforced, and what the planned CSAM screening stage will and will not do.
security.csam.title: CSAM & content screening (in development)
security.csam.body: This is where CIND3R3LLA is going, and it is not there yet. The design: every image and video is hashed at receipt, independently of consent, and compared against databases of known abuse material. A match is quarantined, encrypted, withheld from every public path and preserved for the authorities, never quietly deleted, because deleting a match destroys the evidence that makes a prosecution possible. Today the storage and quarantine machinery is built and no detection provider is connected, so no screening runs. Note the limit that will remain even once it does: hash matching detects known material only. It cannot detect new material, and a no-match result is not a statement that anything is safe.
security.tile1.title: Passwordless
security.tile1.body: Passkeys (WebAuthn / FIDO2): device-bound, phishing- and brute-force-resistant. No shared passwords, nothing to leak or reuse.
security.tile2.title: Your data stays yours
security.tile2.body: Least-privilege and isolated. With the planned local AI, screening and conversations never leave your infrastructure, and there is no third-party processor to trust.
security.tile3.title: Reporting & takedown
security.tile3.body: A second line after screening: anyone can report published content. The operator reviews and removes it, and every action is audit-logged.
security.vuln.title: Found a vulnerability?
security.vuln.body: Report it privately via the security contact in the repository. We credit responsible disclosure and take every report seriously.

os.lede: CIND3R3LLA's core is free software under AGPL-3.0. Run it yourself, read every line, and hold us to what this site claims. Trust should be verifiable, not promised.
os.repo.title: The repository
os.repo.body: Source, issues, roadmap discussions, and the security policy live on GitHub. Contributions are welcome, from typo fixes to whole capabilities, and every change lands in the open.
os.why.title: Why AGPL-3.0
os.why.body: An archive asks for trust. The AGPL guarantees that anyone operating a modified CIND3R3LLA must publish those modifications, so the public can always inspect the code that handles public conversations. That guarantee is the license doing its job.

home.cap.ai.title: Local AI runtime
home.cap.ai.body: Inference runs against your own Ollama endpoint, with independent model routing for intent classification and for reply wording. Connections are probed before activation, a missing model refuses to activate, and when the model is unavailable the deterministic rule engine answers. There is no silent cloud fallback.
home.cap.identities.title: Multi profile identities
home.cap.identities.body: One embedded core hosts many persistent profiles without one process per bot. Actor type, automation mode, personality, permissions, avatar source and public role are separate settings: a fantasy avatar does not decide whether an identity is human operated, autonomous or purely technical.
home.cap.npcs.title: NPCs and characters
home.cap.npcs.body: Autonomous characters host games, explain features, welcome new members, tell context aware jokes and create roleplay moments. Scheduling, permissions, context access, message limits and cooldowns are deterministic. The model supplies the wording, never the decision.
home.cap.agents.title: Human operated agents
home.cap.agents.body: A moderator works through a persistent avatar, discusses difficult situations with the team in a private staff space, refines the behaviour, and continues in the public conversation as the same identity. Assisted mode, autopilot and immediate human takeover, with approval requirements and an audit history.
home.cap.memory.title: Consent first community memory
home.cap.memory.body: Opted in conversation becomes a searchable public archive the community owns. Publication is derived from consent on every read rather than stored as a flag, so a withdrawal takes effect everywhere at once, and the member then chooses whether their words are hidden or destroyed.
home.cap.admin.title: Administration platform
home.cap.admin.body: Every capability has a real control, a stored setting shown separately from its effective runtime state, audit coverage and documented failure behaviour. No hidden behaviour, and no controls that are not wired to anything.
home.cap.safety.title: Moderation and safety
home.cap.safety.body: Public reporting, an operator review queue, audited takedowns, evidence holds that defer destruction without ever delaying hiding, and quarantine that moves material out of the served tree entirely.
home.cap.selfhost.title: Self hosted under AGPL
home.cap.selfhost.body: Your server, your database, your models, your rules. The source is AGPL 3.0, so anyone operating a modified version owes their users the same freedoms. No cloud dependency and no vendor in the middle of your community.
home.control.title: The model never gets authority
home.control.lede: This is the line the whole architecture is drawn around. AI may classify a message and phrase a reply. It never receives permission to execute, to change consent, to publish, or to send arbitrary messages. Identity, permissions, routing, publication and execution stay in deterministic application code.
home.control.point1: A responsible human stays behind every supervised identity and can observe, interrupt, edit, approve or take over at any moment.
home.control.point2: A human operated identity is never silently converted into an autonomous one.
home.control.point3: Nobody can publish or unpublish on another member’s behalf, not an administrator, not the operator, not the model.
